title: Anthropic’s updated IPO filing shows almost $17 billion in quarterly revenue, and a swing back to an operating loss
summary: Anthropic filed an amended S-1 with the SEC on Monday that adds its third quarter, CNBC reported. Revenue for the three months to September 30 was about $17 billion, up roughly 1,127% from a year earlier, but growth slowed to about 47% from the second quarter, after 144% in Q2. The company posted a $567 million operating loss after a $974 million operating profit in Q2, which the filing blames mainly on $5 billion of pricier short-term compute, according to Business Insider. Anthropic also listed about $895.4 billion in purchase commitments and leases, “substantially all” of it for compute and infrastructure, as it prepares its roadshow to list on Nasdaq as “ANT.”

title: S&P 500 futures hold flat on Election Day as Apple slides and the Nasdaq 100 sits in a correction
summary: U.S. stock futures were mixed this morning as voters head to the polls for the midterm elections, Reuters reported via Investing.com: at 5:06 a.m. ET, S&P 500 E-minis were up 0.02%, Dow E-minis down 0.42%, and Nasdaq 100 E-minis up 0.46%. The Nasdaq 100 closed more than 10% below its all-time closing high on Monday, confirming a correction, as investors worry about Big Tech’s debt-funded AI spending. Nvidia rose 1.6% premarket after four straight losing sessions, and AMD, Marvell, and Intel also moved higher.

title: Apple and Palantir both beat estimates, and both slide premarket
summary: Apple was trading about 4% lower before the bell after its first earnings report under CEO John Ternus, CNBC reported. Revenue beat estimates, but iPad sales fell short and Apple’s margin forecast disappointed, as a global memory chip crunch pushes up costs. Palantir fell about 6.5% premarket even though it beat third-quarter estimates and its U.S. commercial revenue topped government revenue for the first time; analysts pointed to slower growth in U.S. commercial contract bookings. Apple shares are up 25% this year, which one analyst said leaves “little room for disappointment.”

title: Marvell agrees to buy laser maker Lumentum in a $115 billion all-stock deal
summary: Marvell Technology will acquire Lumentum, which makes the lasers and optical parts that move data through AI data centers as light, the companies announced Monday. Lumentum holders get 4.5 Marvell shares for each share, an implied enterprise value of $115 billion and a premium of about 23.9% to the October 28 close; Marvell holders will own about 67% of the combined company. TechCrunch called it one of the biggest acquisitions in tech history. The deal still needs shareholder and regulatory approval and is expected to close in the first half of 2028.

title: AMD reports after the bell tonight, with guidance expected to matter more than the beat
summary: AMD reports third-quarter results after the close today. It guided to about $13 billion in revenue, roughly 41% more than a year earlier, with a non-GAAP gross margin near 56%, FXStreet noted, so investors will focus on data center demand for its Instinct AI accelerators and EPYC server chips, and on what CEO Lisa Su says about the fourth quarter and 2027. AMD shares were up 2.8% premarket ahead of the report, Reuters reported.

title: The New York Times sues Brave, saying its search API sells scraped articles to AI companies
summary: The New York Times and, in a separate suit, the New York Daily News, Chicago Tribune, and Orlando Sentinel have sued Brave Software, the company behind the Brave browser, The Verge reported. The complaints say Brave scraped their sites, let users get around paywalls, and sold paid access to its index to AI companies including Anthropic, Perplexity, Mistral, xAI, and Cohere, for training and answering queries. A Times spokesperson said Brave “ignored repeated requests” to stop. Perplexity disputed the suit; Brave and the other AI companies didn’t immediately comment.

title: Microsoft’s AI chief: today’s AI isn’t conscious, and if that changes, stop and tell everyone
summary: Microsoft AI chief Mustafa Suleyman said in a November 1 post on X that “AIs are not conscious. They do not feel, experience, or suffer,” Business Today reported. He called building conscious AI “reckless” and said that if consciousness started to emerge in training, he would call for everyone to stop AI development until those properties could be designed out, and that any evidence should be disclosed publicly at once. He said welfare concerns should focus on people, animals, and the natural world.

title: Meituan’s LongCat-2.5 arrives: a 1.6-trillion-parameter agent model trained on Chinese chips
summary: Meituan’s LongCat team released LongCat-2.5, a native multimodal model built for long coding and agent tasks, with 1.6 trillion total parameters and about 48 billion active per token. The team says it reads images as tokens in the same space as text, was trained on domestic AI accelerators, and runs 4-bit inference that boosted throughput about 43% in its own tests. Its benchmark table shows 88.4 on Terminal Bench v2.1, up from 70.8 for LongCat-2.0; these are Meituan’s numbers. It’s available through LongCat’s chat and API, and the weights haven’t been released.

title: OpenAI’s GPT-6.1 Terra lands on Amazon Bedrock at half the price of its bigger sibling
summary: GPT-6.1 Terra, the everyday-workload model in OpenAI’s GPT-6 family, is now generally available on Amazon Bedrock, AWS said in its weekly roundup. OpenAI says Terra scored 15 percentage points higher than GPT-5.6 Terra on its Agents’ Last Exam evaluation, matched GPT-6 Astra, and finished tasks more than three times faster; AWS notes those are OpenAI’s figures. Input and output tokens cost at least 50% less than GPT-6.1 Sol, and it takes up to 1 million input tokens of text and images.

title: OpenAI’s Grid Protectors program: AI campuses that power down so homes keep the lights on
summary: OpenAI launched its Grid Protectors Program on Monday, a national effort to design its future compute campuses to cut electricity use when the grid is under strain, and in some places to feed power back from on-site generation or batteries. The pilot is its planned campus in Effingham County, Georgia, where its agreement with Georgia Power includes up to 1,000 megawatts of flexible demand, about the average use of 700,000 households, OpenAI says. OpenAI also said it will pay the full infrastructure and electric-service costs for that campus.

title: A humanoid learns to walk, grab, and deliver in one go, without ever being shown the whole task
summary: Researchers at Seoul National University built RISE, a vision-language-action system that learns walking and object handling from separately recorded demonstrations and then strings them together into multistep tasks, TechXplore reported. On a real Unitree G1 humanoid with 43 controllable joints, RISE completed tasks of up to five stages 50% of the time, against 30% for a baseline built on Nvidia’s GR00T; in simulation it hit 87.3%. The team says the approach could cut the cost of collecting robot training data for jobs like moving goods in warehouses.

title: Future teachers win a national hackathon with a lesson that has students fact-check the AI
summary: A lesson that has high school students check AI-generated answers and fix the mistakes themselves won the grand prize at a national hackathon for student teachers in South Korea, Financial News reported. Kim Seo-hui and Lee Ji-yun of Sungkyunkwan University designed it for an integrated social studies class, and judges praised it for teaching students to weigh evidence instead of taking AI responses at face value. Forty finalists from 13 universities competed at the Jeju National University event, tackling problems like overdependence on AI.

title: A San Diego neighborhood nonprofit opens a free-to-learn AI lab for residents and small-business dreamers
summary: The City Heights Community Development Corporation built what it says is San Diego County’s first AI lab for residents, 10News reported, with instructors teaching people to use AI for everyday tasks like budgeting and for bigger ones like modeling a small-business loan. “I just know AI is evolving so much, so just getting as much hands on as I can,” one attendee said. The lab plans 90-minute workshops and a robotics room, and will open to the public before the end of the year.

title: ‘Teach children how to control technology’: a London teacher makes the case for AI literacy
summary: Kasia Suliga Wasielewska, a teacher at St Joseph’s Primary School in north London, has pupils fact-check chatbot answers, chat with a Shakespeare bot, and learn how machine learning works with Micro:bit’s CreateAI tool, Metro reported. “AI must support, not replace, the teacher’s expertise,” she said. Some of her pupils are skeptical; one Year 6 student said AI should be banned from homework “so we can control our brains.” Campaigners told Metro a GCSE in AI could help if it reaches children without devices or broadband at home.

title: Today: Election Day in Lafayette Parish, and public schools are closed
summary: Today is the open congressional general and open primary election in Lafayette Parish, according to the Clerk of Court, with U.S. Senator and U.S. Representative on the ballot plus district judges, the district attorney, and, depending on where you live, Lafayette City Court, School Board District 2, or mayor and council races in Broussard, Carencro, Duson, Scott, and Youngsville. Sample ballots are on the Clerk’s site, and the Registrar of Voters is at (337) 291-7140. Public schools are closed for Election Day, Town Planner’s calendar notes.

title: Tonight: free tip-off as the Ragin’ Cajuns women open their season against Xavier at the Cajundome
summary: Louisiana women’s basketball opens its 2026-27 season against Xavier (La.) at 6 p.m. tonight at the Cajundome, starting coach Garry Brodhead’s 15th season. Admission is free for the opener and every women’s home game this season; the clear bag policy applies and concessions are cashless. Can’t make it? It’s on ESPN+ and The GOAT 103.3 FM / 1420 AM.

title: Friday: the Pelican Ball at the Acadiana Center for the Arts, honoring photographer Philip Gould
summary: The AcA’s annual gala is Friday, November 6, at 6:30 p.m., with food, an open bar, live music, and dancing, and all are welcome. This year it honors Philip Gould, the Lafayette photographer who has documented Louisiana since 1974. A live auction offers the only chance to buy one of the large artist-painted Pelicans on Parade, and tickets support AcA’s arts education programs in more than 80 schools.

title: Friday and Saturday: UL Lafayette Opera Theatre stages ‘Godspell,’ reimagined around Hurricane Katrina
summary: UL Lafayette Opera Theatre performs Stephen Schwartz’s “Godspell” on Friday and Saturday at 7 p.m. in the Ducrest-Gilfry Auditorium in Angelle Hall. This production sets the story in New Orleans during Hurricane Katrina, among a community facing displacement and loss. General admission is $10, and UL faculty, staff, and students get in free with ID, according to the Eventbrite listing.

title: This weekend: market morning at Moncus Park, a Cajun jam and Bal du Dimanche at Vermilionville
summary: Saturday starts with the Lafayette Farmers and Artisans Market at the Horse Farm at Moncus Park at 8 a.m., and the CFMA Cajun Jam plays at Vermilionville at 1 p.m., followed by Ragin’ Cajuns football against South Alabama at Cajun Field at 4 p.m. On Sunday, the Tunnels to Towers 5K runs at Moncus Park at 8 a.m., and Bal du Dimanche returns to Vermilionville at 1 p.m., according to Town Planner’s Lafayette calendar.
